facts.statement: The species Paraprotopteryx gracilis was named and described in 2007 by Zheng Xiaoting, Zhang Zihui, and Hou Lianhai.
facts.quote: In 2007, the type species Paraprotopteryx gracilis was named and described by Zheng Xiaoting, Zhang Zihui and Hou Lianhai.

facts.statement: The genus name Paraprotopteryx means "near Protopteryx" because it resembles that genus.
facts.quote: The generic name means "near Protopteryx", in reference to a presumed similarity with that genus.

facts.statement: The specific name gracilis is intended to mean "pretty".
facts.quote: The specific name is intended to mean "pretty".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen STM V001 consists of a skeleton with a skull mounted on a plate and counterplate.
facts.quote: The holotype is specimen STM V001. It consists of a skeleton with skull on a plate and counterplate.

facts.statement: The species description relies on rump parts where preserved feathers indicate the specimen was a subadult.
facts.quote: The description is based on the rump parts. Feathers have been preserved. The rump represents a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested in 2008 that the fossil correlates with beds dated to approximately 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: While much of the Huajiying Formation underlies the Yixian Formation, Ji and colleagues suggested in 2008 that the Qiaotou Member correlates with the Dawangzhangzi beds of the Yixian Formation, dated to approximately 122 million years ago by Zhou Zhonghe in 2006.

facts.statement: Paraprotopteryx possessed a Y-shaped furcula with a narrow angle between the clavicles.
facts.quote: Paraprotopteryx would have had a furcula (wishbone) which is shaped like a Y with a narrow angle between the clavicles.

facts.statement: The bird had an unusually shaped breastbone that distinguished it from other enantiornitheans.
facts.quote: It also was described as having an unusually shaped breastbone, distinguishing it from other birds in the Enantiornithines.

facts.statement: The carpometacarpus was only partially fused in this species.
facts.quote: The carpometacarpus is only partially fused.

facts.statement: Paraprotopteryx had four rectrices ten centimeters long that more than doubled its total body length, potentially marking an important step in feather evolution.
facts.quote: Paraprotopteryx has four, ten centimetres long, rectrices (flight feathers on the tail), more than doubling the total body length, which may represent an important step in feather evolution.

facts.statement: The tail feathers had very elongated ribbon-like shafts with barbs and expansion only at the tips.
facts.quote: They have a very elongated ribbon-like shaft and only the tips are barbed and expanded.

facts.statement: While the second pair of ribbon-like rectrices is certain, some researchers suspect it might be the result of artifice.
facts.quote: However, although the presence of two ribbon-like rectrices is certain (as in the related enantiornithean bird Protopteryx) the describers of Shanweiniao in 2012 voiced a suspicion that the second pair of rectrices in Paraprotopteryx might be the result of artifice.

facts.statement: Paraprotopteryx belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes.
Paraprotopteryx is classified under the class Reptilia.
The time range for Paraprotopteryx is the Hauterivian, from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Investigations revealed that fossil traders had attached the skull of a different individual to the torso of the holotype.
rejected.quote: The investigation preceding the description of the species proved that fossil traders had added the skull of a different individual to the torso.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'skull of a different individual to the torso'
